name: God creates light and separates day from night
summary: God speaks light into existence and separates it from darkness on the first day.

name: God separates the sky from the seas
summary: God forms an expanse to separate the waters above from the waters below.

name: God creates land, plants, and living creatures
summary: God gathers the waters so dry land appears, then fills the earth and seas with plants and creatures.

name: God creates man and woman in his image
summary: God creates humanity, male and female, in his own image and blesses them to rule over creation.

name: God rests on the seventh day
summary: Having finished his work, God rests on the seventh day and blesses it.

name: God places Adam in the Garden of Eden
summary: God forms the man from the dust and sets him in the garden to work and keep it.

name: God creates Eve from Adam's rib
summary: Seeing that Adam has no fit companion, God fashions Eve from his rib while he sleeps.

name: The serpent tempts Eve to eat the forbidden fruit
summary: The serpent convinces Eve that eating the forbidden fruit will not bring death but wisdom.

name: Adam and Eve eat the forbidden fruit
shortName: Adam and Eve eat the fruit
summary: Eve eats the fruit of the forbidden tree and gives some to Adam, who eats it too.

name: God confronts Adam and Eve
summary: God questions the couple, hears their excuses, and pronounces judgment on the serpent, the woman, and the man.

name: Adam and Eve are exiled from the garden
summary: God clothes Adam and Eve and sends them out of the garden, guarding the way to the tree of life.

name: Cain and Abel bring offerings to God
summary: Cain offers produce and Abel offers the firstborn of his flock, but God favors Abel's offering.

name: Cain murders Abel in the field
summary: Angered by God's rejection of his offering, Cain kills his brother Abel in the field.

name: Cain is cursed and settles in the land of Nod
summary: God confronts Cain, curses him to wander, and marks him for protection before he settles east of Eden.

name: Seth is born to Adam and Eve
summary: Adam and Eve have another son, Seth, in place of the murdered Abel.

name: Enoch walks with God and is taken away
summary: Enoch is noted as walking faithfully with God before being taken away without dying.

name: Noah is born to Lamech
summary: Lamech names his son Noah, hoping he will bring relief from the toil of the cursed ground.

name: God grieves human wickedness and resolves to send a flood
shortName: God resolves to send a flood
summary: Seeing the earth filled with corruption and violence, God decides to judge it with a flood.

name: Noah builds the ark according to God's instructions
summary: Noah follows God's detailed instructions to build a great ark for his family and the animals.

name: God instructs Noah to gather his family and the animals
summary: God tells Noah to bring his family and pairs of every kind of animal into the ark.

name: Noah's family and the animals board the ark
summary: Noah, his wife, his sons and their wives, and the animals enter the ark just before the rain begins.

name: The flood covers the whole earth
summary: Rain falls for forty days and rising waters cover even the highest mountains.

name: All other life on land is destroyed
summary: Every living thing outside the ark perishes in the flood, leaving only Noah and those with him.

name: Noah sends out a raven and doves
summary: Noah releases a raven and then doves to test whether the floodwaters have receded.

name: Noah and his family leave the ark
summary: With the ground now dry, Noah, his family, and the animals finally leave the ark.

name: Noah builds an altar and offers sacrifices
summary: Noah builds an altar and offers sacrifices, and God resolves never again to curse the ground because of humanity.

name: God blesses Noah and permits eating meat
summary: God blesses Noah's family, renews the command to multiply, and now permits them to eat meat.

name: God sets the rainbow as a covenant sign
summary: God promises never again to destroy the earth with a flood and sets the rainbow as the sign of that covenant.

name: Noah's drunkenness leads to Canaan's curse
summary: After Noah becomes drunk and is seen by Ham, he pronounces a curse on Ham's son Canaan.

name: The descendants of Noah's sons spread into nations
summary: The genealogy of Shem, Ham, and Japheth traces how their descendants spread out into distinct nations.

name: Nimrod builds a mighty kingdom in Shinar
summary: Nimrod becomes a mighty warrior and establishes a notable kingdom in the land of Shinar.

name: The people build a city and tower at Babel
summary: The people settle in Shinar and set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens.

name: God confuses their language and scatters them
summary: God confuses the builders' language so they cannot understand one another and scatters them across the earth.

name: The line from Shem to Abram is traced
summary: A genealogy traces the descendants of Shem down to Abram's family in Ur of the Chaldeans.

name: Terah's family sets out from Ur and settles in Haran
summary: Abram's father Terah leads the family from Ur toward Canaan but settles instead in Haran.

name: God calls Abram to leave Haran for Canaan
summary: God calls Abram to leave his country and family for a land he will show him, promising to bless him.

name: Abram builds an altar at Shechem
summary: Arriving in Canaan, Abram builds an altar to the LORD who appeared to him there.

name: Abram deceives Pharaoh about Sarai in Egypt
summary: Fearing for his life during a famine, Abram tells Pharaoh that Sarai is his sister, leading to trouble in Egypt.

name: Abram and Lot separate over land disputes
summary: Growing herds cause strife between their herdsmen, so Abram lets Lot choose land first, and Lot picks the plain near Sodom.

name: God renews his land promise to Abram
summary: After Lot departs, God tells Abram to look in every direction, promising all the land to his offspring.

name: Abram rescues Lot from raiding kings
summary: When a coalition of kings captures Lot in a raid on Sodom, Abram pursues and defeats them to rescue him.

name: Melchizedek blesses Abram after the battle
summary: The priest-king Melchizedek brings out bread and wine and blesses Abram, who gives him a tenth of the spoils.

name: God promises Abram offspring as numerous as the stars
summary: God assures childless Abram that his own offspring will be his heir and as numerous as the stars.

name: God's covenant with Abram sealed by a smoking pot and torch
summary: God formally seals his covenant with Abram as a smoking pot and flaming torch pass between divided animal pieces.

name: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram
summary: Frustrated by years without children, Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram to bear a child in her place.

name: An angel promises Hagar many descendants through Ishmael
summary: Fleeing Sarai's harsh treatment, Hagar meets an angel who promises her son Ishmael will have many descendants.

name: God renames Abram and Sarai as Abraham and Sarah
summary: God changes Abram's and Sarai's names to Abraham and Sarah, marking their new role in his covenant.

name: God institutes circumcision as the covenant sign
summary: God commands circumcision for every male in Abraham's household as the ongoing sign of the covenant.

name: Three visitors announce Sarah will bear a son
summary: Three visitors tell Abraham that Sarah will have a son within the year, and Sarah laughs in disbelief.

name: Abraham intercedes for Sodom's righteous
summary: Abraham pleads with God to spare Sodom if even a small number of righteous people can be found there.

name: Angels rescue Lot's family from Sodom
summary: Two angels urge Lot and his family to flee the city before it is destroyed.

name: Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed and Lot's wife becomes a pillar of salt
summary: God rains destruction on Sodom and Gomorrah, and Lot's wife is turned to a pillar of salt for looking back.

name: Lot's daughters bear sons through their father
summary: Believing no other men remain, Lot's daughters scheme to preserve their family line through their father.

name: Abraham again claims Sarah is his sister before Abimelech
summary: Abraham repeats his earlier deception, telling King Abimelech that Sarah is his sister rather than his wife.

name: God warns Abimelech in a dream to return Sarah
summary: God appears to Abimelech in a dream, warning him that Sarah is a married woman, and he returns her unharmed.

name: Isaac is born to Sarah in her old age
summary: Sarah gives birth to Isaac exactly as God had promised, bringing her laughter after years of waiting.

name: Hagar and Ishmael are sent into the wilderness
summary: At Sarah's insistence, Abraham sends Hagar and Ishmael away, and God provides for them in the wilderness.

name: Abraham makes a treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba
summary: Abraham and Abimelech settle a dispute over a well and make a treaty of peace at Beersheba.

name: God tests Abraham by commanding Isaac's sacrifice
summary: God tests Abraham's faith by commanding him to offer his son Isaac as a burnt offering on Moriah.

name: An angel stops Abraham and provides a ram
summary: Just as Abraham raises the knife, an angel stops him, and a ram caught in a thicket is offered instead.

name: Sarah dies in Hebron
summary: Sarah dies at the age of one hundred twenty-seven, and Abraham mourns for her in Hebron.

name: Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah as a burial site
summary: Abraham negotiates with the Hittites to buy the cave of Machpelah as a burial place for his family.

name: Abraham sends his servant to find Isaac a wife
summary: Abraham sends his chief servant back to his homeland to find a wife for Isaac among his own relatives.

name: Rebekah offers water to the servant and his camels at the well
summary: Rebekah's generosity at the well fulfills the sign the servant had prayed for in choosing a wife for Isaac.

name: Rebekah agrees to marry Isaac and journeys to Canaan
summary: Rebekah agrees to leave her family and travels to Canaan, where she becomes Isaac's wife.

name: Esau and Jacob are born to Isaac and Rebekah
summary: Rebekah gives birth to twin sons who struggled together in her womb, Esau the elder and Jacob the younger.

name: Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for stew
summary: Famished from hunting, Esau trades his birthright to Jacob for a simple bowl of stew.

name: Isaac repeats Abraham's deception about his wife before Abimelech
summary: Like his father before him, Isaac claims Rebekah is his sister out of fear while living among the Philistines.

name: Isaac makes peace with Abimelech over disputed wells
summary: After conflicts over wells his father had dug, Isaac grows wealthy and eventually makes peace with Abimelech.

name: Jacob disguises himself to steal Isaac's blessing
summary: With Rebekah's help, Jacob disguises himself as Esau and receives the blessing Isaac intended for his older son.

name: Esau vows revenge and Jacob flees toward Haran
summary: Furious at being deceived, Esau vows to kill Jacob once their father dies, so Jacob flees to Haran.

name: Jacob dreams of a stairway to heaven at Bethel
summary: On his journey to Haran, Jacob dreams of a stairway reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending.

name: God repeats the covenant promises to Jacob
summary: In the dream, God repeats to Jacob the same promises of land and blessing given to Abraham and Isaac.

name: Jacob meets Rachel at the well
summary: Jacob arrives in Haran, meets Rachel at a well, and falls in love with her.

name: Laban tricks Jacob into marrying Leah first
summary: After Jacob works seven years for Rachel, Laban substitutes Leah on the wedding night instead.

name: Jacob's sons are born through Leah, Rachel, and their servants
summary: Through competition between his wives and their servants, Jacob fathers eleven sons and a daughter.

name: Joseph is born to Rachel
summary: After years of barrenness, Rachel finally bears a son, Joseph.

name: Jacob negotiates spotted and speckled flocks from Laban
summary: Jacob strikes a deal with Laban over speckled and spotted livestock, and his own flocks grow strong.

name: Jacob secretly flees from Laban with his family
summary: Sensing growing hostility from Laban's sons, Jacob quietly leaves Haran with his wives, children, and flocks.

name: Jacob and Laban make a covenant at Gilead
summary: After Laban pursues and confronts Jacob over his stolen household idols, the two men make a covenant of peace.

name: Jacob sends gifts ahead to appease Esau
summary: Fearful of meeting Esau again, Jacob sends generous gifts of livestock ahead to appease his brother.

name: Jacob wrestles with a man and is renamed Israel
summary: Jacob wrestles all night with a mysterious man who blesses him and renames him Israel.

name: Esau runs to greet and reconcile with Jacob
summary: Rather than seeking revenge, Esau runs to meet Jacob, embraces him, and the brothers reconcile.

name: Jacob buys a field from the sons of Hamor
summary: Jacob arrives safely in Canaan, settles near the city of Shechem, and buys a plot of land there.

name: Dinah is assaulted by Shechem, a local prince
summary: Jacob's daughter Dinah is assaulted by Shechem, the son of the region's ruler.

name: Simeon and Levi avenge Dinah by slaughtering the men of Shechem
summary: Simeon and Levi deceive the men of Shechem into circumcision, then attack the city to avenge their sister.

name: Jacob purifies his household and builds an altar
summary: Obeying God's command, Jacob leads his household back to Bethel and builds an altar there.

name: Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin
summary: On the way to Ephrath, Rachel dies giving birth to her second son, Benjamin.

name: Isaac dies and is buried by Jacob and Esau
summary: Isaac dies at an old age, and his sons Jacob and Esau bury him together.

name: Esau's descendants become the nation of Edom
summary: A genealogy records Esau's wives and descendants, who settle in the hill country of Seir and become Edom.

name: Joseph's dreams of ruling provoke his brothers' hatred
summary: Joseph's dreams of his family bowing to him, along with his father's favoritism, deepen his brothers' hatred of him.

name: Joseph is sold into slavery and taken to Egypt
summary: Joseph's brothers throw him in a pit and then sell him to traders who carry him off to Egypt.

name: Tamar is denied her promised husband by Judah
summary: After two of Judah's sons die, Judah withholds his third son from Tamar, leaving her without an heir.

name: Tamar tricks Judah into fathering her children
summary: Disguised as a prostitute, Tamar tricks Judah himself into fathering the children she was denied.

name: Joseph rises to oversee Potiphar's household
summary: Joseph earns Potiphar's trust and is placed in charge of his entire household in Egypt.

name: Potiphar's wife falsely accuses Joseph and he is imprisoned
summary: After Joseph refuses her advances, Potiphar's wife falsely accuses him, and he is thrown into prison.

name: Joseph interprets the cupbearer and baker's dreams
summary: Joseph correctly interprets the dreams of two fellow prisoners, Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker.

name: The cupbearer forgets Joseph after his release
summary: The cupbearer is restored to his position as Joseph predicted but forgets to mention Joseph to Pharaoh.

name: Joseph interprets dreams of seven fat and seven thin years
summary: Finally remembered by the cupbearer, Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams as warning of coming years of famine.

name: Pharaoh elevates Joseph to govern Egypt
summary: Impressed by Joseph's wisdom, Pharaoh places him in charge of all Egypt to prepare for the famine.

name: Joseph stores grain during seven years of plenty
summary: During seven years of abundance, Joseph oversees the storing of massive grain reserves across Egypt.

name: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt for grain
summary: Famine drives Joseph's brothers to Egypt to buy grain, where they bow before Joseph without recognizing him.

name: Joseph tests his brothers and keeps Simeon hostage
summary: Joseph accuses his brothers of spying and holds Simeon hostage until they bring back Benjamin.

name: The brothers return to Egypt with Benjamin
summary: Judah guarantees Benjamin's safety, and the brothers return to Egypt with him as Joseph required.

name: Joseph hosts his brothers and seats them in birth order
summary: Joseph hosts his brothers at a feast, seating them in exact birth order to their astonishment.

name: Joseph plants his cup in Benjamin's sack
summary: Joseph secretly has his silver cup hidden in Benjamin's sack to test his brothers' loyalty.

name: Judah offers himself in place of Benjamin
summary: When Benjamin is accused, Judah pleads for their father's sake and offers to remain as a slave instead.

name: Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers
summary: Overcome with emotion, Joseph reveals to his stunned brothers that he is the one they sold into slavery.

name: Joseph sends for his father Jacob to come to Egypt
summary: Joseph forgives his brothers and sends them back to bring their father Jacob to live in Egypt.

name: Jacob's family travels to Egypt
summary: With God's assurance, Jacob sets out with his entire household and possessions for Egypt.

name: Joseph reunites with his father Jacob
summary: Joseph rides out to meet his father in Goshen, and the two are reunited after many years apart.

name: Joseph settles his family in Goshen and presents them to Pharaoh
summary: Joseph settles his family in the fertile land of Goshen and presents his father to Pharaoh.

name: Joseph manages Egypt's food supply during the famine
summary: Joseph oversees the sale of grain across Egypt, acquiring land for Pharaoh as the famine deepens.

name: Jacob adopts and blesses Joseph's two sons
summary: Nearing death, Jacob adopts Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh as his own and blesses them.

name: Jacob crosses his hands to favor the younger son
summary: Despite Joseph's objection, Jacob deliberately crosses his hands to bless the younger son ahead of the older.

name: Jacob blesses and prophesies over his twelve sons
summary: Jacob gathers his twelve sons and speaks a distinct blessing and prophecy over each of them.

name: Jacob dies and is prepared for burial
summary: Jacob instructs his sons to bury him in Canaan, then dies among his family in Egypt.

name: Jacob is buried in the cave of Machpelah
summary: Joseph and his brothers carry Jacob's body back to Canaan and bury him in the family tomb.

name: Joseph reassures his brothers that God meant their evil for good
summary: Fearful after Jacob's death, the brothers ask forgiveness, and Joseph assures them God used their evil for good.

name: Joseph dies in Egypt at the end of Genesis
summary: Joseph lives to see his descendants before dying in Egypt, asking that his bones be carried to Canaan one day.
